title: Aqua Voice vs Siri on Mac in 2026: dictation, privacy, prices and which to pick
metaTitle: Aqua Voice vs Siri on Mac in 2026: dictation, privacy, prices
description: Aqua Voice vs Siri on Mac in 2026: Aqua Voice is built for dictation and Siri for assistant tasks. Compare prices, privacy and platforms. Pick by job.
secondaryKeywords: aqua voice vs siri on mac
aqua voice or siri for dictation
intro: Aqua Voice is a dictation tool that writes your speech at the cursor in apps that accept pasted text. Siri is Apple's built-in voice assistant, and its newest version, Siri AI, is still in beta. Choose Aqua Voice for dictation. Choose Siri for personal search and actions inside Apple apps. Lazur is included as a third option.
tldr: Aqua Voice is the stronger dictation tool. Its own benchmark claims 97.4% key-term accuracy, which is a company figure.
Siri is the stronger assistant for personal search and actions in Apple apps. Siri AI is still in beta.
Apple lists no price for Siri. Aqua Voice Pro costs $10/month billed annually or $12/month billed monthly.
Lazur is a Mac voice assistant that points at things on screen when you hold ⌥ ⌘. Dictation with fn is included.
Test both on your own apps and vocabulary before you commit to a plan.

blocks.text: Aqua Voice vs Siri at a glance

Aqua Voice and Siri solve different problems. Aqua Voice is a dictation tool. You hold a key, speak, and the words appear at your cursor in the app you already use. Siri is a voice assistant. It answers questions, searches your personal context across apps and takes actions in Apple apps such as Messages, Music and Reminders.

Pick by job. If you write by voice most days, Aqua Voice is built for that work. If you want one assistant that knows your Apple apps, Siri is closer to that goal. Both take your voice, which is why people put them side by side.

This page also covers Lazur, a voice assistant for the Mac. Lazur appears as a third option. Its facts come from its own product description. Its dictation is included, but it is not the headline feature.
Dictation: how each app types your words

Aqua Voice is the stronger dictation tool on paper and in early reviews. Its homepage says it writes into any app that pastes text at the cursor. It adds live grammar refinement, a custom dictionary for names and technical terms, writing styles and support for 49 languages.

Be careful with the accuracy figure. Aqua Voice reports 97.4% key-term accuracy for its Avalon model on AISpeak-10. That is its own English technical-speech benchmark. On the same test it reports 65.1% for Whisper Large v3. Treat both numbers as the company's claim, not an independent test.

Reviews agree the product is fast and accurate. Product Hunt shows a 5.0 rating from 16 reviews, including founder reviews, so the sample is small. A reviewer on Aestumanda calls it the most accurate and productive dictation tool they have used. That is an opinion. The same reviewer says it can pick up nearby TV or other voices.

Siri handles writing differently. Apple's Siri page lists Write with Siri among its features. The page does not describe Siri as a dictation tool for every app. Open Notes, Mail and your browser, then test both tools in the places you actually type.

Lazur's dictation works the same way at a high level. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Lazur also keeps snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Those help if you repeat the same phrases all day.
A quick test you can run on your Mac

Open a blank note and dictate the same paragraph in each tool. Include two names and one technical term. Count the fixes you make afterward. Aqua Voice's custom dictionary is the feature to check for names. Siri's result depends on the app you test in.

blocks.title: Load your names first
blocks.text: Add client names, colleague names and product terms to Aqua Voice's custom dictionary before you judge accuracy. A fair test needs your own vocabulary.
Assistant features: where Siri is stronger

Siri is the stronger assistant. Apple's page lists a conversational assistant, personal context search across apps, actions in Messages, Music and Reminders, and a Siri app that syncs conversations across devices. It also lists Siri in CarPlay and Write with Siri.

Reviewers praise Siri's personal context search and its conversation. One aggregator, Fello AI, paraphrases early coverage calling the new Siri the first in years worth talking to. The same article calls Apple Intelligence helpful, but not a big change. Both lines are opinions, and the article paraphrases unnamed coverage.

Aqua Voice's assistant features are narrower. Its Max plan adds Voice Commands. An Aestumanda reviewer says the app lacks advanced voice navigation features. If you want a tool that answers questions or takes actions in Apple apps, Siri fits better than Aqua Voice.
Where Lazur fits in this comparison

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Lazur points. It does not click for you.

Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click. This suits people who want to learn an app rather than hand it over. Say you need the Reply button in Mail. Ask Lazur, and it circles the button. You click it.

Lazur also handles everyday actions by voice. These include timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music and volume, opening apps and links, web search and Shortcuts. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension, then returns a summary and a report.

Aqua Voice fits long dictation sessions better. Siri fits personal search and Apple app actions better. Lazur fits on-screen help and step by step guidance better. Pick the tool for the job you do most.
Pricing: what each app costs in 2026

Aqua Voice has a free tier with 1,000 words. Its pricing page lists Pro at $10/month billed annually or $12/month billed monthly. Pro removes the word limit and adds Custom Instructions and a Personal Dictionary. Max costs $19/month billed annually or $24/month billed monthly. It adds Realtime Mode and Voice Commands.

Business is $19 per seat per month billed annually, or $24 per seat per month billed monthly, with a 2-seat minimum. Students get 70% off Pro and Max with a school email. Check the pricing page for current terms before you buy.
Older reviews quote different prices. An Aestumanda review from 2025 lists $8 a month. That predates the current pricing page, so trust the company page for the current figure.

blocks.title: Siri has no price yet
blocks.text: Apple lists no price for Siri AI. Apple says expanded access to certain features will be available for a fee in the future. Do not budget for it as free.

Lazur has a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. Pro costs $18/month, or $15/month billed annually, and includes 150 AI actions. Power costs $120/month, or $96/month billed annually, and includes 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both.
A cost example for daily dictation

Say you dictate most days and rarely ask for help on screen. Aqua Voice Pro gives you unlimited words for $10 to $12 a month. Lazur Pro includes unlimited dictation too, but it caps AI actions at 150. Count how often you use the assistant side before you choose.
Many people compare monthly prices and skip annual billing. Both Aqua Voice and Lazur list lower prices when you pay yearly. Check whether the yearly rate fits your budget before you compare the two.
Privacy: what each company says about your data

Aqua Voice says it has a SOC 2 Type II audit report and ISO 27001 certification. It says it is GDPR and HIPAA compliant. Protected health information needs a Business Associate Agreement signed in the app. The Max and Business plans include it. Business also adds Zero Data Retention.

Aqua Voice's homepage says Privacy Mode stores nothing on its servers. It does not say whether transcription runs on your Mac or in the cloud. A Product Hunt reviewer says the app needs network access. Ask the company or check its Trust Center before you rely on offline use.

Apple says Apple Intelligence and Siri AI are designed to protect your privacy at every step. Its Private Cloud Compute section says your data is never stored and used only for your requests. Apple's newsroom says personal data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.

Lazur says it listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Memory of what you asked stays on the Mac.

Each company makes different claims. Aqua Voice points to audits and retention settings. Apple points to its server design. Lazur points to when it listens. Read the claim that matches your risk. Check the contract terms if you handle client or patient data.
Platforms and where each one runs

Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Aqua Voice runs on macOS, Windows, iPhone and Android, according to its homepage. Older Product Hunt reviews asked for iOS and Linux clients, so check the current app store listing.

Siri AI is in beta on iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27 and visionOS 27. It needs an Apple Intelligence device set to a supported language. Apple lists English, French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish at launch.

Apple's newsroom says the most advanced on-device model needs at least 12GB unified memory on an iPad (M4) or a Mac (M3) or later. Siri AI is not available in China or for users under 13. Third-party sources list different chip requirements, so use Apple's device list.
Edge cases: noise, names and mixed languages

Noisy rooms are the first edge case. The Aestumanda reviewer says Aqua Voice can transcribe nearby TV or other voices. Use a headset with a close microphone when you dictate in a shared space. It cuts the pickup of other voices.

Names are the second edge case. Aqua Voice's custom dictionary is built for names and technical terms. Siri's page does not describe a custom dictionary, so expect more corrections there. Lazur's personal dictionary can hold names too, so test it before you rely on it.

Mixed languages are the third. Aqua Voice lists 49 languages. Siri AI starts in six languages, so check yours before you switch. Lazur's facts do not list a language count. Test it in your own language first.
Mac setup: shortcut conflicts and first-day mistakes

Lazur uses ⌥ ⌘ for on-screen questions and fn for dictation. macOS has its own Dictation settings. Open System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation and check which key starts it. If macOS and Lazur both use fn, change one of them.
Siri has its own settings in System Settings > Siri & Spotlight on the Mac. Check them before you build a habit. Look in Aqua Voice's settings for its shortcut before you run your first test.
The most common mistake is running several voice tools at once. Each one listens for its own key, and the results can overlap. Use one tool per job, and quit the rest while you test.
Speed and error rates: what the research shows

A 2016 study from Stanford and the University of Washington compared speech with keyboard entry on touchscreen phones. Speech was 2.93 times faster for English, at 153 words per minute against 52. The study covered short messages, not long documents.

Speech left more errors in the final text. The uncorrected error rate was 1.30% for speech and 0.79% for the keyboard. Speech had a lower corrected error rate, at 5.30% against 11.22%. Proofread dictated text before you send it.

A 2017 Pew survey found that 46% of U.S. adults used digital voice assistants such as Siri, Alexa, Google Assistant or Cortana. 42% used them on a smartphone. I found no newer overall adult figure, so treat it as an older snapshot.
The mistake with the 2.93 figure

People quote the 2.93 figure as if it applies to every task. It does not. The study measured short messages on phones. Your speed in Aqua Voice or Siri depends on your vocabulary, your app and how much you correct.
Who should pick Aqua Voice

items: You dictate long emails, documents and chats most days.
You work on Mac, Windows or phones and want one dictation habit everywhere.
You need a custom dictionary for names and technical terms.
You need team billing or single sign-on. Those sit on the Business plan.

blocks.text: Who should pick Siri

items: You live in Apple apps and want personal search across them.
You want a conversational assistant on your iPhone, iPad, Mac or Apple Watch.
You can wait for Siri AI to leave beta and accept its daily usage limits.

blocks.text: Who should pick Lazur

items: You want help finding things on screen, with a circle and a label.
You want guidance one click at a time, so you learn the app.
You want background research that runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs.

blocks.text: Mistakes people make when choosing

items: Judging dictation from a demo instead of your own paragraph.
Assuming Siri handles dictation in every app. Test Write with Siri in your apps.
Trusting the $8 price from older reviews. Use the current pricing page.
Treating Aqua Voice's 97.4% as independent. It is a self-reported benchmark.
Forgetting the daily usage limits on server-side Siri features.

blocks.text: What to do next

items: Start Aqua Voice on its free tier, which includes 1,000 words, and dictate a real email.
Open Siri's settings on your Mac and check whether your device supports Siri AI.
Start a Lazur trial to test on-screen help. The trial runs 3 days with no credit card. You can [download Lazur](/download) to begin.
Run the same tasks in each app, then keep one tool per job.

blocks.text: If you want a closer look at one pair, read [Lazur vs Siri](/compare/lazur-vs-siri). The choice gets clearer once you have dictated a few real messages in each tool.

faq.question: Is Aqua Voice better than Siri for dictation on a Mac?
faq.answer: For dictation, yes, based on the evidence here. Aqua Voice is built for it, and its homepage lists a custom dictionary, live grammar refinement and 49 languages. Apple's Siri page lists Write with Siri but does not describe Siri as a dictation tool for every app. Test both in the apps you use.

faq.question: How much does Siri cost in 2026?
faq.answer: Apple does not list a price for Siri AI on its Siri page or in its newsroom release. Apple says expanded access to certain server-side features will be available for a fee in the future. Do not assume it stays free. Check Apple's Siri page before you plan a budget.

faq.question: How much is Aqua Voice Pro?
faq.answer: Aqua Voice's pricing page lists Pro at $10/month billed annually or $12/month billed monthly. Pro gives you unlimited words. Max costs $19/month billed annually or $24/month billed monthly. Older reviews that quote $8 a month predate the current page.

faq.question: Does Aqua Voice work without internet?
faq.answer: Reviewers say it needs network access. Its homepage does not say whether transcription runs on your Mac or in the cloud. Do not assume offline use. Ask the company or check its Trust Center before you rely on it with poor signal.

faq.question: Is Siri AI available in every country?
faq.answer: No. Apple says Siri AI is not available in China. It will not initially be available in the EU on iOS, iPadOS or watchOS. It is not available for users under 13. Check Apple's device and region list before you plan around it.

faq.question: Can Lazur replace Siri?
faq.answer: Lazur covers some of what Siri does. It answers out loud, points at things on screen and runs everyday actions such as timers and Reminders. It does not click buttons or operate other apps for you, so you still make the final click.

faq.question: Which one keeps my data more private?
faq.answer: Each company makes different claims, so compare them on the terms that matter to you. Aqua Voice cites SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, and says Privacy Mode stores nothing on its servers. Apple cites Private Cloud Compute. Lazur says it listens only while you hold the shortcut.

verdict: Pick Aqua Voice if dictation is most of your voice work, or if you need Windows or phones too. Pick Siri if you live in Apple apps and can accept a beta with daily limits. Pick Lazur if you want on-screen guidance and step by step help on your Mac. Many people use two of these, one for writing and one for answers.
